subject: science
intro: An adaptation is a heritable trait that helps a population survive and reproduce in its environment. Natural selection leads to adaptation: when individuals with a helpful trait survive and reproduce more, that trait becomes more common over generations, so the population becomes better suited, or adapted, to its environment. For example, in a cold climate, animals with thicker fur survive better, so over time the population tends to have thicker fur. Adaptation is the result of natural selection acting over many generations.

steps: An adaptation is a trait that helps an organism in its environment.
It is a heritable trait that improves survival and reproduction in that environment.
solution.answer: A heritable trait that helps a population survive and reproduce in its environment.

items.prompt: In a cold climate, animals with thicker fur survive better. Explain how natural selection leads the population to become adapted with thick fur.

steps: Thicker fur is a heritable trait that helps survive the cold.
Animals with thicker fur survive and reproduce more, passing on the trait.
Over generations, thick fur becomes common, so the population becomes adapted to the cold.
solution.answer: Thick-furred animals survive and reproduce more in the cold, passing on the trait, so over generations the population adapts to have thick fur.

items.prompt: How does natural selection lead to adaptation over many generations?

steps: Natural selection favors individuals whose traits suit the environment.
Those individuals reproduce more and pass on the helpful traits.
As the helpful traits accumulate over generations, the population becomes adapted to its environment.
solution.answer: Selection favors well-suited traits that are passed on, so over generations the population accumulates them and becomes adapted.

items.prompt: Why must a trait be heritable to become an adaptation?

steps: Adaptation spreads a trait through a population over generations.
Only heritable traits can be passed from parents to offspring.
So a trait must be heritable for selection to pass it on and make it an adaptation.
solution.answer: Because only heritable traits can be passed to offspring, so only they can spread and become adaptations.

items.prompt: A desert plant population develops the ability to store water over many generations. Explain this as an adaptation from natural selection.

steps: Storing water is a heritable trait that helps survive the dry desert.
Plants that store water survive and reproduce more, passing on the trait.
Over generations, water storage becomes common, so the population adapts to the desert.
solution.answer: Water-storing plants survive and reproduce more in the desert, passing on the trait, so the population adapts to store water.

items.prompt: Construct an explanation for how a bird population might become adapted with stronger beaks when only hard seeds are available.

steps: Beak strength is a heritable trait that varies among the birds.
When only hard seeds are available, birds with stronger beaks eat better, survive, and reproduce more.
They pass on the strong-beak trait, so over generations the population becomes adapted with stronger beaks.
solution.answer: Birds with stronger beaks eat the hard seeds better and reproduce more, passing on the trait, so the population adapts to have stronger beaks.
